questions.q: When re-running dbo.usp_CustomerOrderHistory for TrailWorks Co-op after the fix, what does the execution plan show?
options: A single Index Seek against the new covering index, with no Key Lookup operator at all
The same Key Lookup as before, but running slightly faster
A Table Scan replacing the previous Index Seek
The plan is identical to the pre-fix plan
questions.explain: The new covering index eliminates the Key Lookup operator entirely, since every column the query needs is now available at the leaf level.

questions.q: Roughly how much did duration and logical reads improve for the same TrailWorks Co-op execution?
options: From ~28,000 ms / ~118,000 logical reads to ~85 ms / ~350 logical reads — over 300x on both metrics
Duration improved slightly but logical reads stayed the same
There was no measurable change in either metric
Logical reads improved but duration got worse
questions.explain: Both the targeted metrics dropped by more than 300x, matching what the diagnosis predicted for eliminating the Key Lookup.

questions.q: Besides the plan and the raw metrics, what third signal does this lesson check to confirm the fix, and why?
options: Wait statistics — confirming PAGEIOLATCH_SH waits attributable to the query dropped, matching the elimination of scattered page reads
The server's uptime, to confirm no reboot occurred
The number of open browser tabs on the reporting server
The color scheme of the MeridianConnect UI
questions.explain: Chapter 1 warns against declaring victory off a single number — confirming at the wait-stat level too ties the fix back to the original diagnosis.

questions.q: How does this lesson check that the fix didn't create a write-side regression on dbo.Orders?
options: By confirming the redundant old index was dropped, so the table maintains the same number of nonclustered indexes as before, and checking index usage stats for regression
By assuming that any read-side improvement can never affect writes
By disabling all INSERT statements against Orders during business hours
By rebuilding the clustered index as a precaution
questions.explain: Because Lesson 49 dropped the superseded narrow index, the net nonclustered index count didn't increase — and usage stats confirm no measurable INSERT regression.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what makes this a 'verified fix' rather than a change that merely feels faster?
options: Confirmation across four independent signals: the named operator is gone, the baselined metrics dropped by orders of magnitude, the identified wait type dropped, and no collateral write-side damage was found
A single user reporting the screen loads faster now
The fix was applied during a maintenance window
The stored procedure's text got shorter
questions.explain: Verification means checking every specific thing diagnosis named — operator, metrics, waits, and risk of collateral damage — not just a subjective impression.
